newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Air Q4 operating expenses up.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Air Q4 operating expenses up.

text.p: Northwest Airlines Corp said Tuesday its fourth quarter total operating expenses rose to $2.27 billion from $2.11 billion a year ago, reflecting in part a 33.8 percent gain in costs for aircraft fuel, oil and taxes to $389.9 million.
Northwest's total operating revenues gained 6.3 percent to $2.34 billion from $2.20 billion.
The airline's operating margin fell to 3.2 percent for the quarter from 4.1 percent a year ago.

Fourth quarter 1996 results included a $1.5 million gain for employee stock-based compensation, which compares with stock-based compensation costs in the 1995 fourth quarter of $179.2 million. However, salaries, wages and benefits rose to $756.4 million in the quarter from $621.9 million.
Earlier, Northwest reported fourth quarter net earnings of $0.20 a primary share, up from a year-ago net loss of $0.10 a share before a gain for extinguishment of debt.
For the year, Northwest earned $4.93 a primary share before gains, compared with $3.02 a share before gains the year before.

Stock-based employee compensation costs fell to $242.8 million in 1996 from $478.0 million in 1995, while salaries, wages and benefits for the year rose to $2.71 billion from $2.41 billion. Aircraft fuel and other costs for 1996 rose to $1.40 billion from $1.08 billion.
"We had extremely strong traffic, intense competition and sharp fuel price escalation," John Dasburg, Northwest president, said.
Northwest's passenger load factor for the year was 73.1 percent in 1996, up from 71.5 percent in 1995.

"This next year promises to be just as challenging if not more so," Dasburg added. "We will dedicate ourselves in 1997 to remaining focused on our core business and on improving our travel experience for our customers and our workplace for our people."
